description.blurb: Comet Hale-Bopp was visible to the naked eye for 18 months in 1996 and 1997. It has a large nucleus of 37 miles (60 km) and orbits the sun every 2,534 years.
description.more: On July 23, 1995, an unusually bright comet outside of Jupiter's orbit (7.15 AU) was discovered independently by Alan Hale, New Mexico and Thomas Bopp, Arizona. The new comet, designated C/1995 O1, is the farthest comet ever discovered by amateurs and appeared 1000 times brighter than Comet Halley did at the same distance. Normally, comets are inert when they are beyond the orbit of Jupiter, so it has been speculated that Comet Hale-Bopp is either a rather large comet or experienced a bright outburst (or both). The comet is the brightest comet since Comet West in 1976.
